learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic and advanced knowledge of differential and integral calculus for functions of several variables and optimization.
Acquire basic and advanced knowledge of differential and integral calculus for vector-valued functions.
Acquire basic and advanced knowledge of series of functions.
Understand the fundamental definitions, the statements of the main theorems, and the assumptions required for their application.
Be able to apply these tools to solve mathematical analysis problems.
Be able to independently select the most appropriate method for tackling a problem.
Explain theoretical content, procedures, and results using rigorous and appropriate language.
Develop autonomy in learning more advanced mathematical content.
Know the basic techniques of the theory of series of functions, differential and integral calculus, functions of several variables, and vector-valued functions.
Know and understand logical and analytical arguments.
Understand and be able to explain the meaning of complex statements using mathematical notation and language.
Understand the fundamental concepts of analysis and be aware of their potential applications in other fields of study and research.
Be skilled in mathematical reasoning and calculation and be able to understand and apply a theorem.
Be able to read and understand other scientific texts on related topics.
Be able to solve a problem by applying the theorems studied.

syllabus_topics: Series of functions: general theory, power series, and Fourier series.
Differential calculus for real scalar functions of several variables: limits in several variables, partial derivatives, and directional differentiability.
Differential and integral calculus for vector-valued functions: integral calculus on curves and surfaces.
Green's Theorem, Stokes' Theorem, and the Divergence Theorem.
teaching_methods: Face-to-face lessons using a tablet connected to the screen
Individual and/or group discussions with instructor
assessment_rules: The written exam consists of a 120-minute test with six exercises and a section testing understanding of theorems and definitions. To pass the written exam, students must achieve a score of 18/30 or higher. The instructor may request an oral interview for clarification on the written exam, which is optional. Group exercises will be corrected and graded, and their evaluation will contribute to the final grade.
